title: Scaling up and running a time-limited campaign
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Increase outreach volume in a planned way
Run a two-week limited-places campaign with clear terms
Check capacity before promising more work

instruction.heading: Scale on purpose
instruction.body: Once a few customers pay, increase outreach and take on more work. Most of the early gain comes from effort, so plan the hours you can give it without damaging quality.

instruction.heading: Capacity first
instruction.body: Before you promise more jobs, check how many you can deliver well each week, including travel, admin and rest. Business Queensland advises checking your own capacity and deadlines before quoting, and quoting only work you can deliver to the customer's satisfaction. Overbooking can hurt reviews and referrals.

instruction.heading: A limited-places campaign
instruction.body: Run a promotion for a fixed period, with a stated number of places. Be honest: if the places are genuinely limited by your capacity, say so, and open the next round when you have capacity. The ACCC's advertising guide (July 2021; check the current version) expects limited-time offers and short supply to be stated clearly and to be genuinely available. Do not invent scarcity.

instruction.heading: Measure and stop
instruction.body: Track enquiries, bookings, price accepted and quality. Stop or change the campaign when the quality or the margin falls.

procedure: Calculate weekly capacity in hours, including travel and admin.
Set the number of places from that capacity.
Write the campaign terms: dates, places, price and what is included.
Track enquiries, bookings and quality each week.
Close or change the campaign at the end, and report what you learned.

workedExamples.situation: A carpet cleaner has worked out weekly capacity using the first procedure step and wants to run a promotion.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How many places should the campaign offer?
workedExamples.reasoning: Offer no more places than the capacity calculated, and keep a small reserve for repeat customers and quality checks.

commonErrors.prevention: Only state limits that are true.

commonErrors.error: Taking on more jobs than you can deliver well
commonErrors.prevention: Calculate capacity before the campaign starts.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state or territory rules before acting.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Use time-limited offers only when the limit is real.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a limited-places campaign reflect?
Before promising more jobs, what should you check?
options: Only your social media followers today
The size of your logo and your colours
Weekly capacity, including travel and admin
The competitor's reviews and their prices

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a campaign be changed or closed?
options: Only at the end of the year

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to increase outreach and take on more work?
